topic.label: Securities Offerings and Going Public
topic.desc: Raising capital and taking a company public: IPOs, follow-on and secondary offerings, private placements and exempt offerings, bookbuilding and allocation, SPACs and direct listings, and how investors participate.

concepts: Taking a company public: readiness, underwriters, S-1 registration, SEC review, roadshow, pricing and listing.
Offerings after the IPO: follow-ons, secondary sales by holders, shelf registrations, at-the-market programs and block trades.
Raising capital without full registration: Reg D, Rule 144A, Reg S, Reg A+, PIPEs and accredited investors.
How an offering is marketed, the order book built, priced and allocated, and how institutional and retail investors participate.
Alternative paths to public markets: SPAC mergers, direct listings and uplistings.
Issuing bonds and notes: investment grade and high yield deals, indentures, ratings and syndication.
skills: Plans IPO readiness: audits, governance, reporting, underwriters and timeline.
Reads an S-1 or prospectus and summarizes the business, risks, use of proceeds and terms.
Explains follow-on, secondary, shelf, ATM and block trade offerings and when each is used.
Compares Reg D, 144A, Reg S and Reg A+ for a raise by investor type, limits and resale rules.
Explains how an investor participates in an offering: indications of interest, eligibility, allocation and settlement.
Explains the overallotment option and stabilization after pricing.
Compares IPO, SPAC and direct listing by cost, time, dilution and certainty.
Explains a bond offering's process, documents, rating and pricing versus benchmark.
